## Overview

[Jelly](https://jelly-rdf.github.io/) is a compact binary RDF serialization format based on Protocol Buffers. It provides significantly smaller file sizes than text-based formats like Turtle or N-Triples, making it ideal for high-throughput RDF streaming and storage.

RDFLib.jl supports Jelly as a first-class serialization format through `JellyFormat`.

```{julia}
using RDFLib
```

## Serializing Graphs to Jelly

Use the standard `serialize` API with `JellyFormat()`.

```{julia}
# Build a sample graph
g = RDFGraph()
ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")
bind!(g, "ex", ex)

for i in 1:100
    add!(g, Triple(ex("item$i"), RDF.type, ex("Item")))
    add!(g, Triple(ex("item$i"), RDFS("label"), Literal("Item number $i")))
    add!(g, Triple(ex("item$i"), ex("value"), Literal(i)))
end

println("Graph has $(length(g)) triples")
```

```{julia}
# Serialize to Jelly binary format
jelly_data = serialize(g, JellyFormat())
println("Jelly size: $(length(jelly_data)) bytes")
println("Type: ", typeof(jelly_data))
```

## Parsing Jelly Back to Graphs

Parse Jelly binary data back into an RDF graph.

```{julia}
# Round-trip: parse back from binary
g2 = parse_rdf(jelly_data, JellyFormat())
println("Round-trip: $(length(g2)) triples")

# Verify data integrity
sample = first(collect(triples(g2, (ex("item1"), nothing, nothing))))
println("Sample triple: ", sample)
```

```{julia}
# Parse into an existing graph
g3 = RDFGraph()
parse_rdf!(g3, jelly_data, JellyFormat())
println("Merged graph: $(length(g3)) triples")
```

## File I/O

Write Jelly data to files and read them back.

```{julia}
# Write to file
jelly_path = tempname() * ".jelly"
serialize_jelly_to_file(g, jelly_path)
println("Written to: ", jelly_path)
println("File size: ", filesize(jelly_path), " bytes")

# Read from file
g4 = parse_jelly_file(jelly_path)
println("Read back: $(length(g4)) triples")

rm(jelly_path; force=true)
```

## Size Comparison

Compare Jelly against text-based formats.

```{julia}
# Build a larger graph for comparison
g_big = RDFGraph()
ex = Namespace("http://example.org/ontology/things/")
bind!(g_big, "ex", ex)

for i in 1:500
    s = ex("resource_$i")
    add!(g_big, Triple(s, RDF.type, ex("Entity")))
    add!(g_big, Triple(s, RDFS("label"), Literal("Resource number $i"; lang="en")))
    add!(g_big, Triple(s, ex("identifier"), Literal(i)))
    add!(g_big, Triple(s, ex("description"),
        Literal("This is a detailed description of resource $i with some extra text")))
end

println("Benchmark graph: $(length(g_big)) triples")
```

```{julia}
# Serialize in each format and compare sizes
nt_data = serialize(g_big, NTriplesFormat())
ttl_data = serialize(g_big, TurtleFormat())
jelly_data = serialize(g_big, JellyFormat())

println("N-Triples: $(sizeof(nt_data)) bytes")
println("Turtle:    $(sizeof(ttl_data)) bytes")
println("Jelly:     $(length(jelly_data)) bytes")

ratio_nt = round(sizeof(nt_data) / length(jelly_data); digits=1)
ratio_ttl = round(sizeof(ttl_data) / length(jelly_data); digits=1)
println("\nJelly is $(ratio_nt)× smaller than N-Triples")
println("Jelly is $(ratio_ttl)× smaller than Turtle")
```

## How Jelly Compression Works

Jelly achieves compact sizes through:

1. **Dictionary encoding** — repeated IRIs, prefixes, and datatypes are stored once and referenced by ID
2. **Prefix compression** — common IRI prefixes are factored out (like Turtle, but in binary)
3. **Protobuf encoding** — variable-length integer encoding minimizes overhead
4. **Streaming frames** — data is organized into frames for efficient chunked processing

```{julia}
# Control compression parameters
jelly_small = serialize_jelly(g, max_names=64, max_prefixes=8, max_datatypes=8)
jelly_large = serialize_jelly(g, max_names=256, max_prefixes=32, max_datatypes=32)

println("Smaller lookup tables: $(length(jelly_small)) bytes")
println("Larger lookup tables:  $(length(jelly_large)) bytes")
```

## Cross-Language Interoperability

Jelly is a [standardized format](https://jelly-rdf.github.io/) with implementations in multiple languages including Java/Scala (Apache Jena, RDF4J) and now Julia via RDFLib.jl. Jelly files produced by RDFLib.jl can be read by any compliant implementation, and vice versa.

This makes Jelly suitable for:

- **Microservice architectures** — fast binary RPC between services in different languages
- **Data pipelines** — compact intermediate format between processing stages
- **Archival** — space-efficient long-term storage of large RDF datasets
- **Streaming** — frame-based design supports incremental processing

## Summary

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `serialize(g, JellyFormat())` | Serialize graph to Jelly bytes |
| `parse_rdf(data, JellyFormat())` | Parse Jelly bytes to new graph |
| `parse_rdf!(g, data, JellyFormat())` | Parse Jelly into existing graph |
| `serialize_jelly(g; kwargs...)` | Serialize with compression options |
| `serialize_jelly_to_file(g, path)` | Write Jelly to file |
| `parse_jelly_file(path)` | Read Jelly from file |
